thread:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - GPU pool saturation & autoscaler failing to recover. Alerts: queue length > 10k, 429s spike across hotpath pools, tokenbucket drop > 90% in last 5m. Paging oncall.

sara: acked — looking now. seeing steady queue growth on hotpath-gpu. spikes started ~3126499800.

alex: on it with sarah (typo: sara). can you share a quick `kubectl` view for the gpu workers?

sara: running quick checks: `kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-worker -o wide` shows many pods Ready 0/1 or CrashLoopBackoff on nodegroup-hot-1. CPU ok but GPU allocation exhausted.

mike: logs from autoscaler: `autoscalesvc` leader lost heartbeat and then entered cooldown. snippet: ```
2026-06-12T10:12:05Z WARN leader-election timeout
2026-06-12T10:12:07Z ERROR failed to claim lease: context deadline exceeded
2026-06-12T10:12:09Z INFO entering cooldown, backoff 30s
```

alex: that explains lack of new GPU pods. but why 429s? tokenbucket is dropping requests before they hit queue because tier policy reduced burst window during deploy.

jen: incoming from observability: ratepolicy for tier `hotpath` had burst_window set to `1s` during a rolling change 3h ago. That compresses token issuance and creates an effective per-second cap under load.

customer-success: we have customer reports for increased latency and errors. CS says 3 customers on paid tiers are affected. they asked for ETA.

sara: immediate plan: 1) disable strict burst window by rolling back tier change 2) force autoscaler leader re-election / restart autoscaler 3) scale up a temporary hotpath pool with spare non-gpu nodes to accept degraded CPU fallback (if model supports)

mike: executing step 1 — patching ratepolicy: `redwoodctl config set ratepolicy hotpath.burst_window 10s --apply` then `redwoodctl config set ratepolicy hotpath.burst_tokens 500 --apply`. patching now.

alex: while that runs, forcing autoscaler restart on controller nodes: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/autoscaler -n redwood-system`

ops-bot: Triggered `kubectl rollout restart` at 3126500098.

jen: confirm: tokenbucket metrics show token consumption rate rising. previous config: `burst_window=1s, max_tokens=50` new config `burst_window=10s, max_tokens=500`.

mike: patch applied. observability shows immediate drop in 429s from 28% -> 12% in 30s. queue length leveling but still high ~6k. autoscaler restart in progress.

sara: starting temporary scale: `redwoodctl scale --pool hotpath-fallback --replicas 6 --type cpu` — will accept degraded path for some routes.

alex: autoscaler reports successful readiness and leader elected at 3126500204. it immediately starts scheduling additional GPU nodes where available.

mike: additional GPU pods coming up slowly — some nodegroups saturated.

jen: running tokenbucket resync job: `redwoodctl tokenbucket resync --scope hotpath` to reset token counts and avoid negative drift.

ops-bot: tokenbucket resync completed at 3126500250.

customer-success: notified affected customers at 3126500265: initial message sent, promise ongoing updates.

sara: monitoring: 429s down to 3.5%, queue down to 1.2k. CPU fallback pool carrying ~18% of traffic.

alex: followup mitigation checklist to avoid recurrence: 1) lockburst flag in rollout pipeline to prevent accidental 1s windows 2) autoscaler leader TTL increased and add anti-deadlock heartbeat 3) add alert that correlates tokenbucket drop rate + leader-heartbeat-lag to page twice as loud.

mike: I'll open an ops-runbook PR with exact commands we ran, including `redwoodctl` commands and rollback steps.

jen: quick postmortem notes: root cause = combination of (a) burst_window misconfigured to 1s during a config rollout, (b) autoscaler leader briefly lost lease and entered cooldown preventing pod provisioning, and (c) nodegroup capacity fragmentation limited immediate GPU scaling. Consequence = upstream tokenbucket throttling causing 429s and user impact.

sara: immediate action items assigned: mike -> runbook PR + automation to auto-resolve tokenbucket on leader recovery; alex -> autoscaler TTL bump + leader metrics dashboard; jen -> revert pipeline change and add guard; sara -> capacity plan with infra for spare GPU burst pool. ETA for infra plan 48h.

customer-success: thanked the team, customers update scheduled in 2h.

inc-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity lowered to P2 at 3126500348. Please follow the runbook for post-incident review.

mike: note for post-incident: we saw secondary effect: some requests shifted to fallback CPU path and exhibited small regressions in latency and quality. include eval snapshots in the PIR.

jen: agreed. logging this thread into incident tracker and tagging for oncall review.

sara: handing off to alex for post-incident follow-up. alex, you're the incident owner for the PIR.

alex: taking ownership. thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the PIR and schedule a 60m blameless review tomorrow.

customer-success: acknowledged.
